embadon.definition: The numerical measure of a plane or curved surface expressed in unit squares (μονάδες τετράγωνοι), standard throughout Hero's Metrica Book I and Book III.

perimetros.definition: Total boundary length of a polygon or circle; in Metrica I.8, half the perimeter (τὸ ἥμισυ τῆς περιμέτρου, s = (a+b+c)/2) governs the area product Δ² = s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c).

kathetos.definition: The perpendicular dropped from a vertex or apex to the opposite base line or base plane. Metrica I.5–7 compute the altitude via Elements II.12–13, whereas I.8 finds the area directly 'without an altitude' (χωρὶς καθέτου).

pleura.definition: Literally the 'side' of a geometric figure or of an arithmetic square; hence 'take the side of N' (λαβὲ πλευράν) means extract √N, either exactly when rational (ῥητή) or iteratively by Hero's method when irrational.

rhetos.definition: A number possessing an exact integer or fractional root has a 'rational side' (ῥητὴ πλευρά, e.g., √7056 = 84); when it lacks a rational side (e.g., 720 in Metrica I.8), Hero approximates it to arbitrary rational precision 'with minimal difference' (μετὰ διαφόρου ἐλαχίστου).

dynamodynamis.definition: Remarkable algebraic fourth-degree power introduced explicitly by Hero in Metrica I.17 (and implied in I.8's product of two squares ΓΘ² · ΕΗ²), violating strict three-dimensional homogeneity centuries before Diophantus.

itys.definition: The planar ring bounded by two concentric circles of diameters D₁ and D₂; Hero avoids measuring two circles separately in Metrica I.26 by factoring D₁² − D₂² = 4w(D₂ + w) where w = (D₁ − D₂)/2 is the rim width.

speira.definition: Surface and solid generated when a circle perpendicular to a base plane revolves around a fixed coplanar center; measured in Metrica II.13 via Dionysodorus's theorem and by unrolling into a right cylinder of length 2πR.

kolouros.definition: Literally 'dock-tailed' or truncated pyramid or cone cut parallel to its base; in Metrica II.6–10 Hero proves the remarkable decomposition (a + b)/2 squared plus 1/3 of ((a − b)/2)², equivalent to (a² + ab + b²)/3.

ephodikon.definition: Hero's title for Archimedes' heuristic mechanical treatise to Eratosthenes, cited in Metrica I.32, II.14, and II.15 for parabolic areas, the cylindrical ungula (V = d²h/6), and the bicylinder groin vault (V = 2a³/3).

gnomon.definition: Generalized by Hero in Definitiones §58 (Hultsch §59) beyond Euclid II.Def.2: 'Universally, a gnomon is anything which, when added to anything whatever, number or figure, makes the whole similar to that to which it was added.'

anaklasis.definition: The bending back of visual rays from polished mirrors at equal angles, demonstrated in Hero's Catoptrica Prop. 4 from the teleological minimum-path principle that nature acts along shortest lines (διʼ ἐλαχίστων).

dioptra.definition: Hero's precision geared sighting and water-level instrument capable of laying out exact orthogonal sight-lines in horizontal and vertical planes—the ancient ancestor of the modern theodolite.
dioptra.hero_loci: Dioptra Chs. 1–38 (esp. Ch. 15 mountain tunnel, Schöne pp. 238–240)

analogia.definition: Ratio-equality across geometric magnitudes; celebrated in the Preface to Metrica Book III as the sole infallible instrument of proportional justice ('not exceeding or falling short by a single millet-seed').

quadrea.definition: In Rational Trigonometry (Wildberger W.07), the polynomial invariant A(Q₁, Q₂, Q₃) = (Q₁+Q₂+Q₃)² − 2(Q₁²+Q₂²+Q₃²) = 16s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c) = 16Δ², encoding Hero's formula over any commutative ring without square roots.

quadrance.definition: The exact algebraic square on a segment (Euclid's καὶ Ἥρωνος 'τὸ ἀπὸ ΑΒ' / 'δυνάμει δοθεῖσα'), fundamental both to Greek geometric algebra (Metrica III.2: ΑΔ is 'given in square', δοθεῖσα δυνάμει) and to GEOMETOR's exact symbolic verification.

spread.english: rational angle invariant s(ℓ₁, ℓ₂) = sin²θ
spread.definition: Exact rational measure of inclination between two lines in Rational Trigonometry (s = 0 parallel, s = 1 perpendicular), used in geometor.heron to certify Hero's angle bisectors, cyclic quadrilaterals, and equal-angle reflection without transcendental functions.
